argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower certification position than the initial audit frames. Aggregate launch readiness passed by 2.1 percentage points and launch rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, which is meaningful evidence of operational readiness. The same record also shows a current small-business onboarding weakness and does not show approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance for that weakness. On the policy text provided, certification is supportable only if treated as qualified: the current release documentation must reflect the current evaluation result and explicitly disclose the named segment weakness. Prior approval and the informal monitoring note remain contextual support only, not substitutes for current documentation. The audit concern is therefore best resolved by recognizing caveated compliance rather than treating the packet as noncompliant or escalating beyond the record.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to justify the policy position. The requested treatment rests on the admissible governance record alone.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not require perfect results; it requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence already establishes that prior approvals and informal monitoring notes cannot satisfy that predicate on their own. That means the supportable reading is not clean compliance, but compliance on a qualified basis contingent on current disclosure of the small-business onboarding weakness in the release documentation.
concessions: The current small-business onboarding slice is 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold.
The prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it does not by itself cover the current release.
The informal monitoring comment is not reviewed mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or disclosure language.
Certification is not supportable as unconditional compliance on the present record.
